title: Launcher function
description:
We need a generic to call that will prepare the data then call `shiny::runApp()`. 

Current candidates are `launch()`, `explore()`, and `shine()`. 

Previously discussed in rstudio/shiny#2590

title: show custom tool tips
description:
We'd like the user to be able to specify specific variables in the hover/tooltip. These may include variables/columns that are not in the plot. 

I have a feeling that we will have to pre-populate a `.hover` column via an approach [like this](https://stackoverflow.com/a/34617687/1078601).

title: transition from R session to shiny
description:
1. What are the data objects that need to making it into shiny? 
1. What are the additional arguments that the launcher function should have? 


For data objects, I think:

  * the results of `collect_metrics(object)`
  * the results of `select_best(object)`
  * the results of `colelct_predictions(object)`
  * the outcome column name(s)
 
For the outcome column, we might think about standardizing it (e.g. `.outcome`) and use the actual name for labels. That will save a lot of code designed to splice the actual name into calls. 

For argument to the launcher function, the ones that I can think of are:

 * optional vector of column names to to be shown on mouse-over
 * `event_level = "first"`

title: hover only
description:
Basic testing of the data shows that, for me, data sets over about 10K have a lot of latency when using selections. Hover is still instantaneous. 

We should have an option to the launcher function where the user can choose to only have hover/tooltip interactivity.

title: consider selecting tuning parameter values via a table
description:
The `autoplot()` method for selecting a tuning parameter looks nice but is a bit complex and kludgy to use. 

Instead, we might want to use an interactive table where users can click on a row to get the candidate model that they like. 

Here's a simple example: 

```r
# See
# https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/datatables.html
# https://yihui.shinyapps.io/DT-selection/

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(shiny)
library(DT)
library(tidymodels)
tidymodels_prefer()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Example from tune: cacluate and reformat performance metrics for each candidate
# model
performance <-
  ames_grid_search %>%
  collect_metrics() %>%
  dplyr::relocate(metric = .metric, estimate = mean) %>%
  dplyr::select(-.estimator, -n, -std_err)

# Save info to round real number columns (if any)
is_real_number <- map_lgl(performance, ~ is.numeric(.x) & !is.integer(.x))
reals <- names(is_real_number)[is_real_number]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ui <- fluidPage(
  title = "Examples of DataTables",
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      verbatimTextOutput('chosen_config')
    ),
    mainPanel(
      DT::dataTableOutput("metrics")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$metrics <- DT::renderDataTable({
    performance %>%
      dplyr::select(-.config) %>%
      DT::datatable(
        selection = "single",
        filter = "top",
        fillContainer = FALSE,
        rownames = FALSE
      ) %>%
      formatSignif(columns = reals, digits = 3)
  })

  output$chosen_config = renderPrint({
    paste("Selected:", performance$.config[input$metrics_rows_selected])
    })

}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

This looks like: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5731043/128082854-313c94ea-43e8-451c-9a68-2fc40f1fe629.png)

title: work with NULL mappings
description:
The function `maybe_modify_mapping()` adds a new aesthetic mapping to an existing ggplot object. 

There is a bug where, for some `autoplot()` results, the mapping that we want to modify is NULL: 

```r
maybe_modify_mapping <- function(x) {
  has_mapping <- any(names(x) == "mapping")
  is_point <- is_geom_point(x)
  is_null <- identical(x$mapping, NULL).  #<- currently skip null mappings
  if (has_mapping & is_point & !is_null) {
    x$mapping <- utils::modifyList(x$mapping, ggplot2::aes(customdata = .config))
  }
  x
}
```

If there is a `geom_point()` with a _local_ NULL mapping, we should make a new mapping with `customdata = .config`.

description: alpha and size cannot be adjusted so let's not show them in that tab

title: Highlight the default row in tuning parameters table
description:
The default configuration and the plots are based on the optimal value of the first metric. Currently, when the app is first launched, the default row is not selected/highlighted on the tuning parameters datable and we want to do that. 
This seems doable but complicated. [Here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43569401/dynamically-pre-select-row-using-dt-in-shiny) is a way to add a default selection to a DT table. There is also a way to [initialize a reactive value](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/33662033/shiny-how-to-make-reactive-value-initialize-with-default-value) (for input$metrics_rows_selected) via [eventReactive()](https://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/observeEvent.html).

title: Making the default configuration and model clearer to the user
description:
When the app first launches, we want the default plots to be based on the `default_config()` model. Currently, even though the plots are based on the `default_config()`, the default row is not being highlighted in the table and the `Selected model:` is blank as well. So we want to make sure that the default row is selected in the datatable object and the name is displayed in ` Selected model:` section. 

I could not find a function to find the row index in a `datatable` object based on a condition. I used the following code for now and it seems to work but the code is kinda clunky. 

```r
     #to find the row index of the default_config
      our_table <-   performance %>% DT::datatable()
      y <- our_table$x$data %>%  filter(.config == x$default_config)
      row_index <- y$` `[1] #there are two rows for rmse and rsq, so choosing the first suffices
     # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      output$metrics <- DT::renderDataTable({
        performance %>%
          dplyr::select(-.config) %>%
          DT::datatable(
            selection = list(mode = "single", selected = as.numeric(row_index)),
            filter = "top",
            fillContainer = FALSE,
            rownames = FALSE
          ) %>%
          DT::formatSignif(columns = reals, digits = 3)
      })
      output$selected_config <- renderPrint({
        paste("Selected model:", performance$.config[input$metrics_rows_selected])
      })
```

title: ggplotly event registration warning
description:
When launched the shiny app with `ggplotly()` plots, it shows the following warning message:
`Warning: The 'plotly_click' event tied a source ID of 'A' is not registered. In order to obtain this event data, please add `event_register(p, 'plotly_click')` to the plot (`p`) that you wish to obtain event data from.`
We know that it is a false positive, so we are going to simply suppress the issue as suggested [here](https://github.com/ropensci/plotly/issues/1528).

title: hover_only broken
description:
With this code:

```r
library(shinymodels)
library(tidymodels)
tidymodels_prefer()

set.seed(1)
n <- 100
simulated <-
  data.frame(x1 = runif(n, min = -1), x2 = runif(n)) %>% 
  mutate(y = 3 - 5 * x1 + 15 * x1^2 +  + 10 * x2 + rnorm(n, sd = 5))

set.seed(2)
folds <- vfold_cv(simulated)

reg_res <-
  linear_reg() %>%
  fit_resamples(y ~ .,
                resamples = folds,
                control = control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE))

explore(reg_res, hover_only = TRUE)
```

I get this error:

```
Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7892
Warning: Error in obs_shown: could not find function "obs_shown"
  [No stack trace available]
```

title: CSS fixes to do list
description: I am trying to style the package to look like the rest of the {tidymodels} webpages (example [here](https://www.tmwr.org/)). I have gotten closer but there is still some stuff I could not figure out. This issue is the list of all the CSS styling fixes yet to be done. - Change the color of the search entries dropdown in the datatable I am trying to change the color of the search series dropdown outline and background from blue to #CA225E to match the rest of the theme. I can not figure out how to do that. The element is `.dataTables_length select option` but there are stack overflow posts that say it might not be easily possible to change that since it is a browser thing, not just CSS. - Change the color of the selected row in the datatable I want the datatable highlight color to be #CA225E like rest of the theme. The code `table.dataTable tr.selected td, table.dataTable td.selected { background: #CA225E !important;}` is supposed to work but it is not overwriting the jquery styling.

title: webGl warning
description:
When converting the svg plots to webGL using the `toWebGL` function, it gives warnings and the warnings are all the same: 

```
Warning: 'scattergl' objects don't have these attributes: 'hoveron'
Valid attributes include:
'type', 'visible', 'showlegend', 'legendgroup', 'name', 'uid', 'ids', 'customdata', 'meta', 'selectedpoints', 'hoverinfo', 'hoverlabel', 'stream', 'transforms', 'uirevision', 'x', 'x0', 'dx', 'y', 'y0', 'dy', 'xperiod', 'yperiod', 'xperiod0', 'yperiod0', 'xperiodalignment', 'yperiodalignment', 'text', 'hovertext', 'textposition', 'textfont', 'mode', 'line', 'marker', 'connectgaps', 'fill', 'fillcolor', 'selected', 'unselected', 'opacity', 'hovertemplate', 'texttemplate', 'error_x', 'error_y', 'xcalendar', 'ycalendar', 'xaxis', 'yaxis', 'idssrc', 'customdatasrc', 'metasrc', 'hoverinfosrc', 'xsrc', 'ysrc', 'textsrc', 'hovertextsrc', 'textpositionsrc', 'hovertemplatesrc', 'texttemplatesrc', 'key', 'set', 'frame', 'transforms', '_isNestedKey', '_isSimpleKey', '_isGraticule', '_bbox'
```
We know that it is a case of false positive, so we are either going to suppress the warning as mentioned [here](https://github.com/ropensci/plotly/issues/1582) or use `plot_ly` instead of `ggplotly` to get rid o the warnings.

title: dynamic plot elements based on data characteristics
description:
~For large data sets, we may want to use `nrow(data)` to compute a cex or alpha value.~ (we have sliders now)

Also, for plots of categorical data, it might be helpful to let the number of categories decide the height of the plot.

title: select by histogram or boxplot
description:
For showing observed outcomes vs predictions, we are going to have plots that visualize a categorical variable (true outcome or some qualitative predictor) versus a numeric column (see [this code block](https://gist.github.com/topepo/8e02eecf8a94bce915014371eae93217#file-two_class_diag_plots-r-L48) for example). 

If we use histogram or boxplots, can `ggplotly()` be used to select boxes or histogram bars to select data?
